inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The Phase I → Phase II → Excretion flow diagram
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The Drug Metabolism flow diagram: two input rails (Lipophilic drugs at top-left; Polar drugs (water-soluble) at top-right) feeding into Phase I (predominantly CYP450-dependent) and Phase II boxes; Phase I contains the four reaction types (Reduction, Oxidation, Hydrolysis, Methylation) and outputs Slightly polar metabolite (active or inactive) plus Reactive oxygen metabolites; Phase II contains the three conjugation reactions (Glucuronidation, Acetylation, Sulfation) and outputs Very polar, hydrophilic metabolite (except acetylated metabolite); the final Excretion box shows Serum (urine, sweat) and bile (stool) routes. The Phase I output flows into Phase II (sequential) but the page notes the reactions 'do not have to take place sequentially' (eg, phase I can follow phase II, or take place as a single reaction). A vector figure (no raster).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the flow-diagram panel of the DrugMetabolismMap)

inventory.visualPurpose: The Lipophilic-vs-Polar input comparison and the geriatric/slow-acetylator modifier strip
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The Drug Metabolism page's two input rails (Lipophilic drugs → Phase I → Phase II; Polar drugs → Phase II directly) and the two modifier sentences ('Geriatric patients lose phase I first'; 'Patients who are slow acetylators have ↑ adverse effects from certain drugs because of ↓ rate of metabolism (eg, isoniazid)'). The input comparison shows that lipophilic drugs need both phases while polar drugs can skip Phase I and go straight to Phase II conjugation. Pure text + the two modifier callouts.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the input-comparison strip and the geriatric/slow-acetylator callout inside the DrugMetabolismMap) + the rapid-review section in the note

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 252). The Drug Metabolism section has ONE vector flow diagram (the Phase I → Phase II → Excretion flow with the Lipophilic and Polar input rails) — redrawn as ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW vector graphics in the registry visual (no photographs, no copyrighted artwork reproduced). The Phase I / Phase II reaction lists and the lipophilic-vs-polar input split are pure text and are carried verbatim in the note's table blocks (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION). No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. No mnemonic prints on book 230's Drug Metabolism section; the four KYP mnemonics are original designs. NOTE: page 252 (book 230) ALSO contains the Elimination of Drugs section (zero-order vs first-order with the PEA mnemonic); that section is reserved for the separate elimination-of-drugs topic and is NOT covered here.
